description: Baseline capped compat workload harness; profiling points to repeated score_team work, especially personality scoring, Pydantic request construction, and compat skill assignment.
Replace statistics.pstdev-based personality scoring with a float-only one-pass implementation; removes heavy stdlib numeric overhead while preserving output on existing tests.

Add a direct scoring fast path for formation that reuses raw Person objects instead of rebuilding Pydantic TeamQualityRequest/TeamMember structures for every candidate; also cache per-member social preference maps inside team_social_score.

Thread a form_teams-level score cache through candidate generation and swap improvement so repeated task/team evaluations are reused instead of rescored; biggest win comes from improve_allocations reusing candidate scores.

Precompute shortlist-scorer invariants per task to avoid repeated task/preference/weight lookup, but the end-to-end benchmark regressed slightly; remaining cost is dominated more by candidate scoring and compat assignment than by per-person setup.

Cache per-request task lookup and filtered task preferences for score_team, but the improvement was within noise and slightly worse than the current best; static request metadata is not the main bottleneck anymore.

Cache team-only personality and social components across tasks and swap evaluations, then inject them into the direct scoring path; repeated group compositions were paying the same non-task-dependent costs many times.
Cache compat member task-value vectors by member identity and ordered task-skill ids; benchmark improved, but lint failed on a long line so the change was reverted for cleanup before retrying.
Cache compat member task-value vectors by member identity and ordered task-skill ids so repeated candidate teams stop rebuilding the same per-person skill alignment arrays for each task.

Tried a fast-path that skips compat uncovered-skill backfilling when coverage is already complete and only sorts assignments on success, but the benchmark regressed; this helper is not a worthwhile optimization target in the current workload.
Rewrote geometric_mean and weighted_geometric_mean as single-pass log accumulators to remove temporary collections, but the benchmark was slower overall; these helpers are not the next bottleneck.

Use insertion-order team ids instead of sorted ids for the cross-task personality/social cache key. The measured delta versus the current best was effectively noise-level, so this is not worth keeping as an extra behavioral assumption.

Tried collapsing several compat-assignment helper passes into one shared analysis routine, but it changed task assignment behavior on multiple formation regressions and was slower anyway; the helper interactions are more delicate than they look.

Replace compat perfect-matching recursion with a bitmask DP over positive-task masks. Behavior held on the benchmark and speed looked promising, but lint failed on formatting so the change was reverted before validation.

Replaced compat perfect-matching recursion with a bitmask DP over positive-task masks. It preserved checks but regressed the median, so the square-team feasibility check is not a profitable target on this workload.

Thread precomputed task-skill ids, order maps, and max-skills-per-member through compat uncovered-assignment cleanup to avoid rebuilding tiny structures, but the added plumbing slowed the benchmark slightly.

Tried making swap improvement compare objectives from quality lists instead of rebuilding temporary allocation lists, but the extra list churn still lost to the baseline; improve_allocations is not the main remaining bottleneck.

Tried trimming math.isclose calls inside _compat_other_member_best_values with cheaper equality fast paths, but the benchmark regressed and lint rejected the nested-condition style, so this avenue is not promising.

Added a cached task-skill metadata helper so compat scoring could reuse ordered skill ids and sort maps across repeated evaluations of the same task, but the extra cache lookups/regression overhead outweighed the tiny structure rebuilds.

Combined compat task-capability counting with other-member-best analysis so _assign_task_skills_compat can reuse one shared per-task pass; this looked like the strongest improvement so far, but ty rejected the optional counts typing and the change was reverted for a cleanup retry.

Fuse compat member-task analysis into one shared pass (member_has_match + task_capable_counts + other_member_best_values) and reuse the same task_capable_counts in member-priority ordering to remove duplicate scans of the member/task matrix.

asi.hypothesis: Combining compat matrix analyses and eliminating duplicated capable-count passes will cut _assign_task_skills_compat overhead without changing behavior.
asi.result: Slight median improvement with unchanged quality/team-count metrics.

description: Precompute per-member positive task bitmasks and per-task best values in compat analysis, then iterate only positive candidate bits during assignment and reuse precomputed best task values during uncovered rescue scoring.

asi.hypothesis: Bitmask-driven candidate scanning should cut _assign_task_skills_compat inner-loop work by avoiding full task scans and repeated max() rescans.
asi.result: Large median improvement with unchanged quality/team-count metrics.

description: Attempted a fast-path to skip full uncovered-assignment rebalancing when covered_mask already spans all task skills, plus reused a per-call task_skill_order map. This changed compat assignment semantics (missing rescued skill assignments in overlap-heavy cases), so checks failed and the change was reverted.

asi.hypothesis: Bypassing _compat_fill_uncovered_assignments on full coverage should remove unnecessary assignment recounting/sorting overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Fast-path was behaviorally incorrect: it skipped expected compatibility rebalancing that preserves legacy assignment distribution invariants.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep _compat_fill_uncovered_assignments semantics intact; target micro-optimizations inside it (fewer allocations/lookups) rather than skipping it.
asi.failure_surface: tests/test_team_quality.py compat assignment invariance and overlap-coverage checks

description: Precompute task_skill_ids once per compat assignment call and thread that tuple through member-task value caching, member-priority tie-breaking, and candidate priority generation to remove repeated task-id tuple/list reconstruction overhead.

asi.hypothesis: Eliminating repeated task-skill id reconstruction in hot compat loops will reduce per-candidate overhead without behavior changes.
asi.result: Strong runtime win with stable quality/team-count metrics.

description: Threaded precomputed task_skill_ids/task_skill_order through compat uncovered-assignment sorting/filling to avoid rebuilding per-call metadata in _compat_fill_uncovered_assignments, but end-to-end median regressed.

asi.hypothesis: Passing precomputed task-skill metadata into fill/sort helpers would reduce string/dict setup overhead in a hot path.
asi.rollback_reason: Added parameter plumbing and extra argument passing cost more than metadata reconstruction in this workload.
asi.next_action_hint: Revert this helper-plumbing approach; focus on reducing algorithmic work inside _compat_fill_uncovered_assignments or candidate_combinations instead.

description: Added per-task local scored-candidate memoization in build_scored_candidates/greedy_allocations to avoid repeated cached_score_team lookups, but Ruff B023 rejected closure capture of loop-scoped memo dictionaries and the attempt was reverted.

asi.hypothesis: A local memo around scored_candidate should cut redundant cache lookups for the same candidate tuples within each task loop.
asi.rollback_reason: Lint failure (B023) due loop-variable closure capture; benchmark also regressed strongly.
asi.next_action_hint: If retried, bind memo dict via default argument in closure or use functools.partial; only continue if end-to-end metric improves.

description: Tried a unique-task-skill fast path in _compat_fill_uncovered_assignments that uses assigned-skill set coverage to skip full count/decrement bookkeeping when all required skills are present, but the extra set construction/regression overhead made the benchmark slower.

asi.hypothesis: Most compat assignments already cover all unique task skills, so a set-coverage fast path should avoid expensive per-skill counting.
asi.rollback_reason: Fast-path bookkeeping (set build + uniqueness checks) was slower than baseline counting in this workload.
asi.next_action_hint: Avoid extra prechecks in _compat_fill_uncovered_assignments; target lower-level loop/call overhead or different hotspots.

description: Replaced sorted team-id cache keys with request-scoped bitmask signatures for personality/social component caches to avoid per-score tuple sorting, but end-to-end runtime regressed.

asi.hypothesis: Bitmask team signatures should be cheaper than sorting IDs for every score_team cache lookup.
asi.rollback_reason: Extra request-level bit-map lookups and bitwise accumulation outweighed tuple-sort savings on this workload.
asi.next_action_hint: Revert team-signature bitmasking; prioritize proven compat-assignment hotspots instead.

description: Reworked compat member-priority key generation to iterate precomputed positive-task bitmasks instead of full value enumeration, but the extra list/mask handling was slightly slower than the original key comprehensions.

asi.hypothesis: Using member_positive_masks in _compat_member_priority_order should reduce zero-value filtering overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Bitmask/list conversion overhead offset any gains; median regressed versus the current best.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the existing priority-key comprehensions; hunt for wins outside this ordering helper.

description: Changed compat member-task value cache keys from (member_id, task_skill_ids tuple) to identity-based (id(member), id(task_skills)) with object-identity guards to avoid hashing task-skill-id tuples on every lookup, but median runtime regressed.

asi.hypothesis: Identity-based cache keys should make _compat_member_task_values hits cheaper than tuple-of-strings key hashing.
asi.rollback_reason: Extra identity-guard indirection and broader cache tuple payload negated lookup savings; benchmark slowed.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep tuple-key cache design; pursue different hot-path reductions.

description: Skipped per-member sorting in _compat_sort_member_assignments when a member has 0/1 assigned skills, but this micro-optimization regressed end-to-end runtime.

asi.hypothesis: Avoiding sorted() for tiny assignment lists should trim compat assignment overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Branch/check overhead outweighed any saved sorting work on this benchmark.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not add tiny conditional guards around sort; pursue coarser-grained wins.

description: Replaced shortlist reordering in candidate_combinations (dict+sort by input positions) with an input-order filter over selected shortlist IDs, but this was slower end-to-end.

asi.hypothesis: Avoiding per-call position dict construction and sort should reduce shortlist overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Set construction plus full input-order scan cost more than the small sort in this workload.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep existing shortlist.sort path; target heavier work than shortlist ordering.

description: Replaced compat perfect-positive matching check with a member-positive-mask DFS/backtracking solver (sorted by mask sparsity) to avoid float-matrix traversal, but median runtime still regressed.

asi.hypothesis: A bitmask-only perfect-matching feasibility check should be cheaper than augmenting-path traversal over float rows.
asi.rollback_reason: Even with mask precomputation and sparse-first ordering, recursion overhead remained slower on this workload.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep existing matching check; focus on higher-impact hotspots like candidate scoring/selection.

description: Reduced scored shortlist expansion factor from 4 to 1 to cut candidate scoring volume; benchmark improved sharply but this violated shortlist-coverage/caching behavior guarantees and degraded specialist selection quality in regression tests.

asi.hypothesis: Lowering MAX_SCORED_COMBINATION_EXPANSION would materially reduce candidate_combinations work in capped search.
asi.rollback_reason: Behavior changed too much: shortlist expansion tests, cache reuse expectations, and capped specialist-quality regressions failed.
asi.next_action_hint: If revisiting candidate caps, preserve tested expansion semantics (or update tests with a principled algorithm change) rather than tuning the global constant blindly.
asi.failure_surface: tests/test_form_teams.py scored-cap shortlist and specialist-preservation cases

description: Refactored candidate_combinations heap ranking loop to compare score/tie-break scalars before constructing replacement tuples, aiming to reduce per-combination tuple churn, but this regressed median runtime.

asi.hypothesis: Avoiding full entry-tuple construction on non-competitive combinations should speed scored shortlist ranking.
asi.rollback_reason: Extra Python-level branching/indexing cost outweighed tuple-allocation savings.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep original tuple-comparison heap loop; focus on larger-grain reductions in scored candidate volume or scoring cost.

description: Add a fast path in _compat_fill_uncovered_assignments for max_skills_per_member==1 (the common equal-team-size compat case): directly fill uncovered skills into empty members and return without the generic rebalance/sort passes.

asi.hypothesis: When each member can hold at most one task skill, the generic uncovered rebalance loops and final sort are unnecessary overhead.
asi.result: Meaningful median improvement with unchanged quality metrics and passing checks.
asi.branch_frequency: with_uncovered path is dominant in benchmark (~84% of calls)

description: Tried broadening the uncovered-assignment fast-path guard to `len(task_skills) <= len(assignments)` (instead of using computed max_skills_per_member==1), but this variant regressed despite equivalent behavior/checks.

asi.hypothesis: Checking len(task_skills)<=len(assignments) directly would be a cheaper trigger for the one-skill-per-member fast path.
asi.rollback_reason: This guard/flow shape was slower in practice (likely branch/layout effects) versus the prior explicit max_skills_per_member path.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the previous max_skills_per_member==1 fast-path implementation from the kept commit.

description: Attempted to fold compat member-priority tuple precomputation into _compat_member_task_analysis (returning prebuilt scarce/rich priority tuples) and simplify _compat_member_priority_order to index sorting, but this added too much work to the analysis pass and regressed heavily.

asi.hypothesis: Precomputing priority tuples during existing analysis loops would remove repeated member/task scans in _compat_member_priority_order.
asi.rollback_reason: The expanded analysis phase and extra tuple/list allocations outweighed saved scans.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep priority computation separate; avoid heavy tuple materialization in _compat_member_task_analysis.

description: Switch score_cache keys from string-id tuples to object-identity tuples (`tuple(id(person) for person in people)`) to cut hot-path key construction overhead in cached_score_team while keeping per-form-request cache scope unchanged.

asi.hypothesis: Identity-based candidate keys are cheaper to build than repeatedly reading person.id strings for every cached_score_team lookup.
asi.result: Clear median/best improvement with unchanged quality metrics and passing checks.

description: Changed greedy tie-break key to use candidate.people insertion order instead of sorting member IDs per candidate (to reduce per-candidate sorting overhead), but runtime regressed slightly.

asi.hypothesis: Dropping sorted(member.id) in greedy tie-break should save repeated tiny sorts during best-candidate selection.
asi.rollback_reason: The alternate tie-break shape was slightly slower overall and not worth behavioral risk.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep existing sorted-ID tie-break; focus on larger hotspots.

description: Added a fixed-size (len==4) fast path for cached_score_team key construction to avoid generator/tuple-building overhead on the benchmark’s common team size, but median result was effectively unchanged and slightly worse.

asi.hypothesis: Manual tuple construction for 4-person teams should shave overhead from the hottest cache-key path.
asi.rollback_reason: No consistent improvement over the current best; likely within noise/branch overhead.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep generic identity-tuple key path unless a broader small-team specialization proves faster.

description: Make score_cache keys order-insensitive by sorting person object identities (`tuple(sorted(id(person) ...))`) so equivalent teams in different member orders reuse cached score_team results.

asi.hypothesis: Many cached_score_team calls revisit the same team composition in different order; canonicalized keys should increase cache-hit rate enough to offset tiny sort cost.
asi.evidence: Observed ordered-vs-unordered key cardinality gap during instrumentation (~1857 vs ~1765 unique keys per form_teams run).
asi.result: Large improvement with unchanged quality metrics and passing checks.

description: Tried replacing `tuple(sorted(...))` canonical key construction with list-build + in-place `.sort()` in cached_score_team, but this was slower despite equivalent semantics.

asi.hypothesis: List+sort might be a cheaper canonicalization path than sorted(generator) for order-insensitive score-cache keys.
asi.rollback_reason: Extra list allocation/mutation overhead outweighed any generator savings; median regressed.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the tuple(sorted(...)) canonicalization that produced the large cache-hit win.

description: Changed request-level personality/social cache signatures from sorted member ID strings to sorted member object identities, aiming to avoid string-property work in score_team, but this regressed runtime.

asi.hypothesis: Identity-based team signatures should be cheaper than sorting member.id strings for component-cache keys.
asi.rollback_reason: Cache-key identity canonicalization here underperformed; likely due reduced locality/lookup characteristics versus string IDs.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep string-id team signatures for personality/social caches while retaining order-insensitive identity keys for score_cache.

description: Tried conditional canonicalization of score-cache member identity tuples (only sort when IDs are out of order) to avoid unnecessary sorts, but lint rejected zip() without strict= and benchmark performance regressed.

asi.hypothesis: Most candidate tuples are already monotonic by object id, so sorting only on inversions should preserve cache hits while reducing sort overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Implementation hit Ruff B905 (missing strict=) and showed no runtime benefit anyway.
asi.next_action_hint: Abandon conditional-sort variant; keep unconditional tuple(sorted(...)) canonicalization from the kept change.

description: Added dual score-cache lookup (ordered identity key first, canonical sorted key second) and backfilled aliases to avoid sorting on exact-order repeats, but this increased cache bookkeeping overhead and regressed runtime.

asi.hypothesis: Two-tier ordered→canonical cache keys would cut repeated canonical-sort work while preserving order-insensitive reuse.
asi.rollback_reason: Extra dictionary operations/alias writes outweighed saved sorting in this workload.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep single canonical key lookup path (sorted identities) for score_cache.

description: Removed sorted() from score_team’s personality/social cache team signature (using tuple(member.id) insertion order instead), but poorer cross-task cache reuse outweighed the saved sort cost and runtime regressed.

asi.hypothesis: With order-insensitive score_cache keys, score_team could avoid sorting member IDs for component-cache keys.
asi.rollback_reason: Order-sensitive signatures reduced component-cache hit rate enough to outweigh sort savings.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep sorted member-id signatures for personality/social caches.

description: Tried replacing score_cache task key from task_id string to id(task_id) integer identity in cached_score_team, but this regressed runtime.

asi.hypothesis: Integer task identity keys might hash/compare faster than task_id strings in hot score_cache lookups.
asi.rollback_reason: No speedup observed; identity-key variant performed worse.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep string task_id component in score_cache keys.

description: Specialized _assign_task_skills_compat member assignment loop for max_skills_per_member==1 to bypass per-member inner-loop scaffolding, but the duplicated branch path increased overhead and regressed runtime.

asi.hypothesis: A dedicated single-assignment path in _assign_task_skills_compat should reduce inner-loop overhead in the common square-team workload.
asi.rollback_reason: Extra branch duplication and code-path overhead outweighed loop simplification.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep generic member assignment loop; the fill-stage fast path is the profitable specialization.

description: Replaced sorted identity-tuple score_cache keys with request-scoped team bitmask keys (order-insensitive int masks via cached person-id->bit map), but map lookups/bit assembly regressed runtime.

asi.hypothesis: Bitmask team keys should avoid per-call identity sorting while keeping order-insensitive score-cache hits.
asi.rollback_reason: Per-call person_id map lookups and mask accumulation were slower than tuple(sorted(id(...))) in this workload.
asi.next_action_hint: Retain sorted-identity tuple keys for score_cache; bitmasking is not a win here.

description: Inlined individual_fit logic into shortlist_scorers with precomputed task/similarity/preference invariants to avoid repeated per-person lookups, but this increased per-scorer work/allocation overhead and regressed runtime.

asi.hypothesis: Precomputing shortlist invariants once should reduce candidate scoring overhead inside scorer().
asi.rollback_reason: The inlined path added enough Python-level list/sort work that it underperformed the existing function-based path.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep current shortlist scorer implementation; avoid large scorer rewrites unless supported by fresh profiling evidence.

description: Added optional precomputed task/similarity/preferences/weights inputs to individual_fit and wired shortlist_scorers to pass them, but the broader call signature/plumbing overhead regressed median runtime.

asi.hypothesis: Reusing shortlist-level invariants in individual_fit would reduce repeated lookup/resolve work during candidate ranking.
asi.rollback_reason: Extra argument plumbing and branching inside individual_fit offset the intended savings.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the simpler individual_fit call path; avoid adding many optional precompute branches there.

description: Added an early set-based uncovered-skill fast path in _compat_fill_uncovered_assignments for the one-skill-per-member regime (unique task skill IDs + <=1 assignment per member), but extra guards/set work regressed median runtime.

asi.hypothesis: When each member has at most one assignment, uncovered detection can use set membership instead of count/decrement bookkeeping.
asi.rollback_reason: Guard checks and set construction overhead outweighed savings from simplified uncovered detection.
asi.next_action_hint: Stick with the existing max_skills_per_member==1 fast path; avoid additional precheck-heavy branches.

description: Added per-task local scored-candidate memoization keyed by candidate tuple object id in build_scored_candidates/greedy_allocations (with loop-safe default binding) to avoid repeated cached_score_team lookups, but end-to-end runtime still regressed.

asi.hypothesis: candidate_combinations returns the same tuple objects later consumed by callers, so id(candidate)-keyed local memoization should skip duplicate cache lookups cheaply.
asi.rollback_reason: Local memo bookkeeping overhead outweighed saved lookups in this workload.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not add extra per-task memo layers on top of score_cache here.

description: Replaced math.isclose checks with direct float equality in _compat_member_task_analysis (best/second-best tracking and unique-best detection), but this regressed runtime.

asi.hypothesis: Direct equality comparisons on cached compat skill levels should be cheaper than repeated math.isclose calls in hot analysis loops.
asi.rollback_reason: Despite cheaper comparisons, this rewrite slowed end-to-end performance in the benchmark.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep existing math.isclose-based analysis logic; avoid this micro substitution.

description: Switched canonical score-cache identity tuple construction from `sorted(id(person) for person in people)` to `sorted(map(id, people))`, but this alternative was slower in end-to-end runtime.

asi.hypothesis: Using map(id, people) might reduce generator overhead in canonical score-cache key construction.
asi.rollback_reason: No benefit observed; this variant regressed relative to the current best.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the existing `sorted(id(person) for person in people)` implementation.

description: Precomputed explicit social-preference neighbor sets in shortlist_scorers and threaded them into candidate_social_potential to avoid repeated has_explicit_social_preferences scans, but added set/dict overhead regressed runtime.

asi.hypothesis: Replacing repeated preference-list scans with prebuilt neighbor sets would speed candidate_social_potential in compat mode.
asi.rollback_reason: Set materialization/lookups and extra branching were slower than the current path on this workload.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep existing social-potential checks; this precompute strategy is not profitable here.

description: Added request-scoped cache of canonical people-key tuples keyed by tuple-object identity to avoid repeated `tuple(sorted(id(...)))` work in cached_score_team, but cache lookup/identity-guard overhead regressed runtime.

asi.hypothesis: Reusing canonicalized score-cache people keys for repeated candidate tuple objects should cut sort overhead in cached_score_team.
asi.rollback_reason: Extra dictionary and identity-guard bookkeeping outweighed saved key canonicalization cost.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep direct canonicalization path in cached_score_team; focus on larger hotspots such as _compat_member_priority_order or candidate_combinations.

description: Tried reducing tuple materialization in _compat_member_priority_order by keeping priority lists as sorted lists (and switching rich path to generator-based sorted input), but this regressed runtime significantly.

asi.hypothesis: Avoiding tuple(...) wrapping in member-priority keys should cut allocation overhead in a hot compat helper.
asi.rollback_reason: List-based keys and generator shape were slower than the original tuple-based implementation.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep existing tuple-based priority keys; this helper is sensitive to Python comparison/allocation tradeoffs.

description: Replaced full ranking sorts in candidate_combinations with `heapq.nlargest(shortlist_size, ...)` for primary and alternate scorers to avoid sorting entire people lists, but this regressed runtime.

asi.hypothesis: Since shortlist extraction only consumes top shortlist_size entries, nlargest should be cheaper than full sorted(..., reverse=True).
asi.rollback_reason: For this workload (small people lists, many invocations), nlargest overhead outweighed full-sort costs.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep full sorted rankings in candidate_combinations.

description: In _compat_fill_uncovered_assignments, moved max_skills_per_member computation earlier and skipped _compat_sort_member_assignments when no uncovered skills and max_skills_per_member==1 (single-skill lists already ordered), but median runtime still regressed.

asi.hypothesis: Avoiding unnecessary sorting in no-uncovered single-skill cases should shave hot-path overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Reordered branching/math checks did not produce a net win and measured slower end-to-end.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep existing no-uncovered return path; this micro-branch is not worthwhile.

description: Switched order-insensitive score_cache keys from sorted identity tuples to frozensets of person identities to avoid per-call sorting, but frozenset hashing/allocation was slower overall.

asi.hypothesis: frozenset-based team keys could replace sorted-tuple canonicalization with cheaper order-insensitive key construction.
asi.rollback_reason: frozenset creation/hash overhead outweighed saved sort work in this benchmark.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep sorted identity tuple keys for score_cache.

description: Attempted local-binding micro-optimization (`isclose = math.isclose`) inside _compat_member_task_analysis, but introduced a syntax/indentation error and benchmark could not run.

asi.hypothesis: Binding math.isclose locally in the hot analysis helper might reduce function lookup overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Patch introduced IndentationError in scoring.py, causing benchmark crash before measurement.
asi.next_action_hint: Retry only with a clean, syntax-checked local alias patch if still desired.

description: Retried local `isclose` binding optimization in _compat_member_task_analysis, but automated text replacement malformed indentation around conditional branches and benchmark crashed again.

asi.hypothesis: Local-binding `math.isclose` in the hottest compat-analysis loop could reduce global lookup overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Patch application error collapsed line breaks in the if/elif block, causing another IndentationError.
asi.next_action_hint: Use a single block replacement for the full loop section when retrying to avoid malformed partial edits.

description: Tried a gentler scored-combination cap by lowering MAX_SCORED_COMBINATION_EXPANSION from 4 to 3 (instead of 1) to reduce ranking work while preserving semantics, but median runtime regressed.

asi.hypothesis: A smaller but non-extreme scored expansion factor could keep behavior stable while trimming candidate scoring overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Despite passing checks, the median slowed notably versus current best.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep expansion factor at 4 unless a more targeted adaptive policy is introduced with evidence.

description: Attempted adaptive scored-combination expansion (halve expansion when team_size>=4) to reduce candidate enumeration for benchmark-sized teams, but this violated large-team scored-cap invariants and failed candidate_combinations regression checks.

asi.hypothesis: Reducing scored shortlist expansion only for larger teams could preserve most semantics while trimming work on the capped compat workload.
asi.rollback_reason: Adaptive budget under-enumerated combinations for large team sizes, breaking test expectations for candidate cap behavior.
asi.next_action_hint: Any adaptive expansion policy must preserve the `DEFAULT_MAX_CANDIDATE_TEAMS` output-size guarantees in large-team scored-candidate tests.

description: Rewrote compat perfect-matching feasibility check to use precomputed member positive bitmasks with integer seen-mask recursion (augmenting-path style) to avoid float-row scans, but Ruff rejected the explicit loop style (SIM110) and the run was reverted.

asi.hypothesis: Bitmask-based augmenting path matching should reduce overhead in _compat_has_perfect_positive_matching.
asi.rollback_reason: Lint failure (SIM110) blocked validation; benchmark trend was also slower than current best.
asi.next_action_hint: If retried, use lint-compliant `all(...)` form, but prioritize only if profiling shows this check is still worth targeting.

description: Retried local-binding `isclose = math.isclose` in _compat_member_task_analysis via a clean full-block rewrite to remove global attribute lookups in the hottest loop, but end-to-end runtime still regressed.

asi.hypothesis: Local aliasing of math.isclose would reduce lookup overhead across ~1M+ calls in compat analysis.
asi.rollback_reason: Even with a clean implementation and passing checks, the benchmark was slower than current best.
asi.next_action_hint: Drop the local-isclose alias idea; focus on algorithmic reductions rather than lookup micro-optimizations.

description: Added an early return in _compat_sort_member_assignments when all members have <=1 assigned skill (skip task-order map and sorting entirely), but this regressed median runtime despite seeming workload alignment.

asi.hypothesis: In the benchmark, compat assignment lists are usually length 1, so skipping sorting work entirely should speed _compat_sort_member_assignments.
asi.rollback_reason: Additional all(...) scan/branch overhead outweighed saved sorting/mapping work end-to-end.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not add precheck-heavy short-circuits in this helper; keep straightforward sort path.

description: Attempted to cut _compat_member_task_analysis second-pass comparisons by precomputing each task's unique best member index and building other_member_best_values from copied best-values rows with targeted overrides, but lint failed (SIM108) and runtime trend was slower anyway.

asi.hypothesis: Replacing per-member/per-task isclose checks in the second pass with unique-best index overrides would reduce analysis overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Ruff SIM108 style violation in the unique-best update block; benchmark also regressed versus current best.
asi.next_action_hint: If revisiting, use lint-compliant ternary assignment and only proceed if microbench indicates a real gain.

description: Tested order-insensitive score_cache keys based on sorted person.id strings (instead of sorted object identities) to avoid id() calls, but this remained slower than the current best identity-based canonical key.

asi.hypothesis: String-id canonicalization might outperform id()-based key construction while preserving order-insensitive cache hits.
asi.rollback_reason: String sorting/comparison was still slower than the existing sorted identity tuple approach.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep sorted identity key strategy in cached_score_team.

description: Replaced tuple-based candidate priority construction in _assign_task_skills_compat with manual lexicographic scalar comparisons to avoid per-candidate tuple allocations, but this branch-heavy rewrite regressed median runtime.

asi.hypothesis: Eliminating tuple allocation/comparison in the hottest compat candidate-selection loop should reduce overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Manual nested comparisons introduced more Python branch cost than tuple comparisons saved.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep tuple-based priority comparisons in _assign_task_skills_compat.

description: Added a lightweight `precomputed_weights` parameter to individual_fit and passed shortlist_scorers' pre-resolved weights to avoid repeated resolve_weights allocations per person, but this still regressed median runtime.

asi.hypothesis: Eliminating repeated resolve_weights calls in individual_fit should reduce shortlist scorer overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Extra optional-parameter plumbing/branching outweighed savings from skipping resolve_weights.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep individual_fit simple; avoid optional-parameter precompute patterns that add per-call branching.

description: Added request-scoped task lookup cache (`task_id -> Task`) and replaced repeated linear task scans in task_hardness/individual_fit/score_team with dictionary lookups, but this regressed median runtime.

asi.hypothesis: Avoiding repeated `next(... for task in request.tasks)` scans in hot paths should reduce score_team overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Dictionary-cache plumbing and lookups were slower than tiny list scans for this workload's small task count.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep direct task scans; task lookup caching is not profitable here.

description: Tried removing sort work from cached_score_team keys (ordered identity tuples) while canonicalizing swap/replacement teams in improve_allocations via `_canonical_people_tuple(...)`; this reduced cross-order key churn but added heavy tuple sorting in swap loops and regressed badly.

asi.hypothesis: Canonicalizing only swap-generated teams could preserve most order-insensitive cache reuse while avoiding per-call key sorting in cached_score_team.
asi.rollback_reason: Sorting whole team tuples inside improvement loops dominated and made runtime much worse.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep order-insensitive key sorting inside cached_score_team; avoid canonicalizing every swap tuple.

description: Added a 4-person fast path in cached_score_team key canonicalization that skips sorting when object identities are already monotonic (`id0<=id1<=id2<=id3`) and only sorts unsorted quartets, but this branch-heavy path regressed runtime.

asi.hypothesis: Since most 4-person tuples are already monotonic by object id, a direct comparison fast path should beat unconditional sorted(...).
asi.rollback_reason: Extra branching/comparison overhead outweighed savings from skipped sorts.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep unconditional sorted identity tuple canonicalization in cached_score_team.

description: Switched top-partner aggregation in candidate_social_potential and candidate_personality_potential from full `sorted(..., reverse=True)[:k]` to `heapq.nlargest(k, ...)`, but this regressed runtime for the benchmark’s small candidate lists.

asi.hypothesis: Selecting only the top `team_size-1` pair scores via nlargest should beat full sorting in shortlist potential calculations.
asi.rollback_reason: For these small lists, nlargest overhead exceeded full sort slicing performance.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the current sorted-slice implementation in candidate potential helpers.

description: Added a safe early-continue in improve_allocations single-replacement loop: skip objective recomputation when rescored allocation quality is <= current allocation quality (cannot improve lexicographic objective with other teams unchanged), but this regressed runtime.

asi.hypothesis: Many replacement trials are non-improving; bypassing trial list/objective construction for guaranteed non-improvers should reduce improve_allocations overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Extra branch/check overhead exceeded saved objective computations on this workload.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep existing straightforward improvement check; this pruning gate is not profitable.

description: Changed _compat_member_priority_order rich-priority key construction from list-comprehension input to generator input for sorted(..., reverse=True) to reduce intermediate list allocation, but this regressed runtime.

asi.hypothesis: Generator-fed sorted() in rich priority key should reduce allocation overhead in a hot helper.
asi.rollback_reason: Generator path was slower than the explicit list comprehension in this workload.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep list-comprehension sorted input for rich priority keys.

description: Added a len==4 specialization for cached_score_team key canonicalization that sorts an explicit 4-tuple of person identities instead of a generator expression, but this caused a major regression.

asi.hypothesis: Explicit 4-item tuple sorting in cached_score_team could beat generator-based sorted identity canonicalization for the benchmark’s common team size.
asi.rollback_reason: Branching and explicit tuple path performed significantly worse end-to-end.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the original generator-based sorted identity key path.

description: Added a small-combination fast path in candidate_combinations scored mode (full score+sort when C(shortlist,team)<=2*max_candidate_teams; heap only for larger spaces), but this regressed significantly on the benchmark.

asi.hypothesis: For near-budget scored spaces (e.g., 1001 combos for top-1000), full sort should beat per-item heap maintenance.
asi.rollback_reason: Full materialization/sort overhead was worse than the existing heap path.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep heap-based top-k selection in scored candidate_combinations.

description: Bound `other_member_best_values[member_index]` once per member in _assign_task_skills_compat to avoid repeated nested indexing in candidate priority construction, but this regressed runtime.

asi.hypothesis: Reducing nested list indexing in the hot candidate-priority loop should shave compat assignment overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Local-binding change did not help and measured slower end-to-end.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep direct indexing form; this micro-local binding is not profitable.

description: Added a specialized `has_explicit_social_preference_to(...)` helper and replaced singleton-set checks inside candidate_social_potential to avoid per-call `{id}` allocations, but this significantly regressed runtime.

asi.hypothesis: Avoiding singleton-set construction in candidate_social_potential should reduce overhead from frequent social-preference checks.
asi.rollback_reason: The extra helper-call path and preference scan shape performed much worse than the previous implementation.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep existing has_explicit_social_preferences usage in candidate_social_potential; avoid this specialization.

description: Refactored _compat_member_priority_order to define only the needed priority-key closure per call (rich path or scarce path) instead of defining both unconditionally, but this worsened runtime.

asi.hypothesis: Avoiding construction of an unused closure in _compat_member_priority_order should trim helper overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Branching/nested-definition layout regressed performance compared with the original structure.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the original dual-closure implementation; this refactor is not beneficial.

description: Memoized full scorer tuples in shortlist_scorers and changed alternate rankings to read cached personality/social components via `lambda person: scorer(person)[idx]`, aiming to avoid separate alternate scorer work, but this regressed heavily.

asi.hypothesis: Reusing cached primary scorer outputs for alternate ranking keys should reduce shortlist ranking overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Extra scorer-cache lookups and lambda indirection outweighed any saved alternate scoring work.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep dedicated alternate scorer functions; avoid scorer-tuple memo wiring.

description: Removed greedy_allocations temporary list materialization by taking max() directly over scored_candidate generator expressions (both random and deterministic branches), but this regressed runtime.

asi.hypothesis: Avoiding creation of `scored_candidates` lists should reduce allocation overhead in greedy candidate selection.
asi.rollback_reason: Generator-based max path was slower than list materialization in this workload.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep explicit scored_candidates lists in greedy_allocations.

description: Added global cache for square compat perfect-positive-matching feasibility keyed by per-member positive-task masks to reuse _compat_has_perfect_positive_matching results across repeated evaluations, but this regressed runtime.

asi.hypothesis: Perfect-matching feasibility depends only on positive mask structure, so caching by member mask signatures should avoid repeated recursive matching work.
asi.rollback_reason: Cache lookup/signature overhead outweighed avoided matching work on this workload.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not add global perfect-matching cache; keep direct feasibility check.

description: Added request-scoped cache for `has_team_social_preferences` keyed by team signature to avoid repeated explicit-preference scans in compat score_team, but this regressed runtime.

asi.hypothesis: Caching per-team social-preference existence should reduce repeated has_explicit_social_preferences scans across task evaluations.
asi.rollback_reason: Extra cache plumbing/lookups and duplicate team-signature handling outweighed saved scans.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep direct has_team_social_preferences computation path; this cache layer is not worthwhile.

description: Replaced generator-based ranked_lists.extend(...) with explicit append loop for alternate scorer rankings in candidate_combinations, but this regressed runtime.

asi.hypothesis: Avoiding generator-to-extend overhead when building alternate ranked lists could slightly reduce candidate_combinations setup cost.
asi.rollback_reason: Explicit append loop was slower in this benchmark.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep original extend(generator) form for ranked_lists construction.

description: Switched cached_score_team canonical key construction from `sorted(generator)` to `sorted(list-comprehension)` for person identities, but this regressed runtime.

asi.hypothesis: Materializing identity values via list comprehension before sorting might outperform generator-based sorted in cached_score_team.
asi.rollback_reason: List-comprehension variant was slower than the current generator-based implementation.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep generator-based sorted identity key construction.

description: Added safe pair-swap pruning in improve_allocations (skip objective recomputation when both swapped team qualities are <= their originals), but this regressed heavily.

asi.hypothesis: Many pair swaps worsen both teams; skipping trial allocation/objective work for these cases should reduce improve_allocations cost.
asi.rollback_reason: The additional branch and comparisons in the innermost swap loop outweighed saved objective calculations.
asi.next_action_hint: Avoid extra pruning checks in improve_allocations without stronger evidence.

description: Replaced repeated integer ceil divisions (`math.ceil(len(a)/len(b))`) with pure-integer formulas (`(len(a)+len(b)-1)//len(b)`) across compat/partitioned assignment helpers, but this regressed runtime.

asi.hypothesis: Integer ceil formulas should avoid float conversion overhead in hot assignment-size calculations.
asi.rollback_reason: Arithmetic rewrite did not translate to speedup and was slower end-to-end.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep original math.ceil-based expressions in assignment helpers.

description: Added a near-budget scored-candidate special case in candidate_combinations for `C(shortlist, team_size) == max_candidate_teams + 1` (score all, drop single worst, then sort) to avoid heap maintenance, but this regressed strongly.

asi.hypothesis: When scored combinations exceed budget by only one, direct drop-worst selection should be cheaper than heap-based top-k maintenance.
asi.rollback_reason: Full materialization/min+sort work was slower than the existing heap path.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep current heap-based top-k selection even in near-budget cases.

description: Added request-scoped cache for `valid_person_ids` and reused it in individual_fit/score_team instead of rebuilding `{candidate.id}` sets per call, but this regressed runtime.

asi.hypothesis: Caching request-wide valid person IDs should reduce repeated set construction in hot formation/scoring paths.
asi.rollback_reason: Extra cache indirection outweighed tiny set-construction cost in this workload.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep direct local valid_person_ids construction where currently used.

description: Tried replacing sorted-identity tuple score_cache keys with request-scoped identity-bitmask keys (`task_id + team_mask`) using cached `id(person)->bit` mapping to avoid per-call sorting, but this regressed badly.

asi.hypothesis: Bitmask keys built from cached identity bits should provide cheaper order-insensitive score_cache key construction than sorting identities each call.
asi.rollback_reason: Dictionary lookups plus bit accumulation still cost more than sorted identity tuples on this workload.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep sorted identity tuple keys in cached_score_team.

description: Rekeyed compat member-task value cache from `(id(member), task_skill_ids tuple)` to `(id(member), task_signature int)` via a global task-skill-signature table to reduce tuple-of-strings hashing on hot lookups, but this regressed drastically.

asi.hypothesis: Integer task signatures should be cheaper cache-key components than task-skill-id tuples in _compat_member_task_values.
asi.rollback_reason: Global signature lookup/management overhead outweighed any key-hash savings; end-to-end performance collapsed.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep direct tuple-based task-skill keying in _compat_member_task_values.

description: Replaced inline lambda `combination_scorer` callsites with named local `combination_quality(...)` functions in build_scored_candidates/greedy_allocations to reduce lambda call overhead, but this regressed substantially.

asi.hypothesis: Named local scorer functions might execute marginally faster than inline lambdas across thousands of candidate scoring calls.
asi.rollback_reason: Function indirection/layout change performed significantly worse in practice.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep original lambda-based combination_scorer callsites.

description: Reworked candidate_combinations shortlist dedup/order restoration to use per-person index booleans (`seen_positions`) and input-order rebuild instead of id-set + final sort-by-input-position, but this regressed strongly.

asi.hypothesis: Boolean position tracking plus direct input-order reconstruction might be cheaper than set membership + shortlist sort.
asi.rollback_reason: Extra index mapping and full input scan were slower than the original approach.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep existing seen-id set and final shortlist sort path.

description: Tried replacing log/exp geometric_mean with a product-and-root implementation (including fast paths for n=2 and n=4) to reduce math.log overhead, but this changed objective ordering enough to break greedy-fallback improvement behavior tests.

asi.hypothesis: Direct product roots should compute geometric means faster than log/exp in hot scoring paths.
asi.rollback_reason: Numerical behavior changed objective comparisons in swap improvement, causing regression test failure in capped greedy fallback improvement.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep current log/exp geometric_mean for behavioral stability; avoid numerically different formulations.

description: Extended request-level team component cache to include precomputed `valid_person_ids` and reused it in score_team compat task-preference filtering (removing per-score set construction), but this still regressed runtime.

asi.hypothesis: Piggybacking valid_person_ids onto the already-used request cache should save per-call set allocations in score_team with minimal extra overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Added cache tuple size/handling and data access did not pay off; median was slower than current best.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep existing score_team setup; avoid expanding request cache payload for tiny derived sets.

description: Rewrote has_explicit_social_preferences from generator-based any(...) to an explicit for-loop with local bindings to reduce generator overhead in a measured hotspot, but this regressed runtime.

asi.hypothesis: A manual loop with local variable bindings should outperform generator-based any() for repeated social-preference membership checks.
asi.rollback_reason: Despite hotspot targeting, explicit loop form was slower end-to-end.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the original any(...) implementation for has_explicit_social_preferences.

description: Extended has_explicit_social_preferences to accept a single teammate-id string and updated candidate_social_potential to pass ids directly (avoiding singleton-set allocations), but this still regressed runtime.

asi.hypothesis: Avoiding `{id}` allocations in candidate_social_potential by supporting string teammate ids in has_explicit_social_preferences should reduce social-check overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Type-branching and alternate generator path in has_explicit_social_preferences outweighed allocation savings.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep original set-based call pattern for has_explicit_social_preferences.

description: Added pairwise score caches in shortlist_scorers for candidate_social_potential and candidate_personality_potential so symmetric two-person scores are computed once per unordered pair and reused across both member directions; this was close but still slower than the current best.

asi.hypothesis: Caching symmetric pair scores should cut repeated team_social_score/team_personality_score calls during shortlist ranking.
asi.rollback_reason: Despite reducing repeated pair computations, added pair-key/cache bookkeeping left median above current best.
asi.next_action_hint: If revisiting, consider lighter key representation for pair caches or selective caching only for the personality path.

description: Added an identity-keyed pair cache only for candidate_personality_potential (without social-path changes) to reuse symmetric two-person personality scores across both directions, but runtime remained slower than best.

asi.hypothesis: Personality potential recomputes symmetric pair scores; caching by unordered person identity pair should reduce duplicate team_personality_score calls with lower overhead than full social+personality caching.
asi.rollback_reason: Pair-cache bookkeeping still outweighed saved personality pair recomputation.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not pursue pair-score caches in shortlist potentials further unless coupled with a broader ranking redesign.

description: Tried reducing singleton-set churn in candidate_social_potential by prebuilding `{person.id}` and per-teammate singleton-id sets once per call and reusing them in has_explicit_social_preferences checks, but this regressed.

asi.hypothesis: Eliminating repeated `{id}` allocations inside social potential loops should reduce has_explicit_social_preferences overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Building and indexing singleton-set maps introduced more overhead than the original direct literals.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the simpler direct singleton-set usage in candidate_social_potential.

description: Changed scored top-k selection in candidate_combinations to prefill with `islice(..., max_candidate_teams)` + `heapify` (instead of N heappushes for the initial window), then process remainder with heapreplace; this was close but still slower than current best.

asi.hypothesis: Heapifying an initial scored window should reduce top-k maintenance overhead in near-budget scored candidate selection.
asi.rollback_reason: The list materialization + heapify path did not beat incremental heappush/heappreplace in end-to-end runtime.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep existing heap update loop for scored candidate selection.

description: Added equality-first fast paths around math.isclose in _compat_member_task_analysis (`value == best` / `value == second_best` checks before isclose, plus equality short-circuit in unique-best detection), but this regressed runtime.

asi.hypothesis: Many compat values are exact repeats, so equality short-circuits should cut expensive isclose calls in the hottest analysis loop.
asi.rollback_reason: Extra branching and compound conditions outweighed reduced isclose calls; net slowdown.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the simpler existing isclose-based comparisons.

description: In greedy_allocations, bypassed shortlist_scorers/candidate_combinations for uncapped tasks (`C(remaining, team_size) <= max_candidate_teams`) and used direct itertools.combinations instead, to avoid scorer setup on later tasks, but this regressed.

asi.hypothesis: Later greedy tasks often fall below the cap and don't need shortlist machinery, so directly enumerating combinations should save overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Branching and path split overhead outweighed any saved shortlist setup in this workload.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep uniform candidate_combinations usage in greedy_allocations.

description: Bound heap operations to locals (`heappush`, `heapreplace`) inside candidate_combinations scored top-k loop to reduce global attribute lookups, but this regressed runtime.

asi.hypothesis: Local binding of heap functions in the hottest candidate ranking loop should shave Python lookup overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Local-binding micro-optimization did not pay off and measured slower end-to-end.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep direct heapq calls in candidate_combinations.

description: Replaced string/id tie-break components in _assign_task_skills_compat candidate priority tuples with precomputed integer tie ranks (`task_tie_ranks`) to reduce inner-loop tuple comparison cost, but this regressed runtime.

asi.hypothesis: Integer tie-rank comparisons should be cheaper than repeated string/-index tuple components in compat candidate selection.
asi.rollback_reason: Added precomputation and changed comparison shape slowed end-to-end performance.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep original task_skill_id/-task_index tie-break tuple in compat candidate priority.

description: Precomputed full shortlist scorer values for every person once per task (including personality/social potentials) and switched primary/alternate scorer keys to direct tuple lookups, but this regressed versus lazy cached scorer functions.

asi.hypothesis: Materializing per-person scorer tuples once should reduce repeated key-function overhead across primary and alternate rankings.
asi.rollback_reason: Eager precompute and lambda lookup indirection cost more than existing lazy cached scorer closures.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep existing shortlist_scorers lazily cached design; avoid eager full precompute.

description: Added optional `team_signature` field to ScoredAllocation and threaded score_team’s existing sorted-id signature into allocations so greedy deterministic tie-break could reuse it instead of sorting member ids per candidate, but this regressed badly.

asi.hypothesis: Reusing precomputed team signatures from score_team should remove repeated tie-break sorting in greedy candidate selection.
asi.rollback_reason: Larger allocation objects and extra attribute plumbing outweighed tie-break sort savings.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not extend ScoredAllocation for this tie-break optimization; keep existing key expression.

description: Rewrote rich_first_priority_key in _compat_member_priority_order from list-comprehension+sorted into explicit append loop + in-place sort (then tuple conversion) to reduce intermediate construction overhead, but it remained slower than current best.

asi.hypothesis: Manual loop + in-place sort for rich priority tasks might beat nested comprehension/sorted construction in a hotspot.
asi.rollback_reason: Python loop overhead offset any construction savings; median still regressed.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep existing rich_first_priority_key comprehension form unless combined with a larger helper redesign.

description: Added identity-keyed symmetric pair-score cache only in candidate_social_potential (wired from shortlist_scorers) so social pair values are computed once per unordered pair and reused across both directions; result was very close but still slower than best.

asi.hypothesis: Social potential recomputes mirrored pair scores and explicit-preference checks; caching pair results should reduce has_explicit/team_social overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Pair-cache keying and lookup overhead still outweighed saved recomputation on this workload.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not keep social pair cache; if revisited, consider narrower caching keyed by shortlist callsite characteristics.

description: Changed _compat_sort_member_assignments to sort assignment lists in place (`list.sort`) instead of creating new lists via sorted(...) per member, aiming to cut allocations, but it was still slower than best.

asi.hypothesis: In-place sort should reduce per-call list allocations in a frequently called compat helper.
asi.rollback_reason: In-place mutation path did not outperform existing sorted(...) reassignment in end-to-end benchmark.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep existing sorted(...) assignment form in _compat_sort_member_assignments.

description: Attempted greedy-only local scored-candidate memoization keyed directly by candidate tuple objects to avoid repeated cached_score_team lookups after candidate_combinations scoring, but Person objects are unhashable so this crashed.

asi.hypothesis: A local greedy-task memo could bypass duplicate score-cache key canonicalization for already-scored candidate tuples.
asi.rollback_reason: Candidate tuples contain unhashable Person objects, causing TypeError when used as dict keys.
asi.next_action_hint: If retried, key local memo by an explicit hashable identity tuple (e.g., tuple(id(person) for person in candidate)).

description: Retried greedy-only local scored-candidate memoization with hashable identity keys (`tuple(id(person) for person in candidate)`) to avoid duplicate cached_score_team calls after candidate_combinations scoring, but this still regressed.

asi.hypothesis: A local per-task memo should reduce repeated score-cache canonicalization overhead for candidates already scored during combination ranking.
asi.rollback_reason: Extra local key construction/dictionary operations outweighed any saved cached_score_team lookup cost.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not add local memo layer in greedy_allocations; rely on global score_cache only.

description: In candidate_combinations scored top-k path, replaced `ranked.sort(key=lambda item: (item[0], item[1]), reverse=True)` with direct tuple sort `ranked.sort(reverse=True)` since `(score, -index, combination)` is already ordered by the desired tie-break components and `-index` is unique.

asi.hypothesis: Removing key-function calls from final heap result sorting should shave overhead in scored candidate selection without changing ordering semantics.
asi.result: Small but real median/best improvement with unchanged quality/team-count metrics.
asi.proof_obligation: `-index` uniqueness preserves deterministic order; direct tuple reverse sort matches previous `(item[0], item[1])` ordering intent.

description: Tried split-phase scored top-k selection in candidate_combinations: prefill heap with first `max_candidate_teams` combinations via `itertools.islice`, then process remainder without per-iteration len checks. This regressed vs current best.

asi.hypothesis: Removing repeated heap-size checks in the scored loop should slightly reduce candidate ranking overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Iterator/islice split and extra control flow outweighed any savings from avoiding len checks.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the original single-loop heap fill/replace structure with direct len check.

description: Inlined singleton-set social-preference checks directly inside candidate_social_potential (local person/teammate preference scans) to avoid has_explicit_social_preferences calls and `{id}` allocations, but this remained slower than best.

asi.hypothesis: Inlining one-to-one preference checks should reduce call/allocation overhead in candidate_social_potential hotspot.
asi.rollback_reason: Inline generator scans and extra local setup still underperformed existing helper-based implementation.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep current helper-based social preference checks.

description: Changed final scored-candidate extraction from tuple-unpacking list comprehension to index-based form (`[entry[2] for entry in ranked]`) after reverse sort, but this regressed heavily.

asi.hypothesis: Index-based list extraction might be marginally cheaper than tuple unpacking in candidate_combinations return path.
asi.rollback_reason: No micro-win; measured substantially slower end-to-end.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep tuple-unpacking comprehension for ranked combination extraction.

description: Tried shrinking scored top-k heap entries in candidate_combinations from `(score, -index, combination)` to `(score, -index)` plus a side dict `index->combination` to avoid carrying combination tuples in heap comparisons/sorts, but dict bookkeeping made it slower.

asi.hypothesis: Smaller numeric heap entries should reduce top-k maintenance overhead if combination objects are stored out-of-band.
asi.rollback_reason: Extra dict insert/pop/lookups outweighed savings from smaller heap entries.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep direct `(score, -index, combination)` heap entries.

description: Added request-scoped cache mapping sorted person-identity signatures to sorted person-id team signatures, and used it in score_team to avoid repeated string signature sorting across tasks. Despite high theoretical reuse, this regressed heavily.

asi.hypothesis: Caching team_signature by identity signature would amortize expensive sorted(member.id) work across many score_team calls for repeated team compositions.
asi.rollback_reason: Extra identity sorting and cache indirection per score_team call outweighed saved string sorts.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not add team_signature cache layer; keep direct team_signature construction.

description: Reworked candidate_combinations shortlist ordering to track shortlist as input indices (append index per selected person, then integer-sort and rebuild shortlist) instead of person list + sort-by-position dict key, but this regressed.

asi.hypothesis: Sorting integer indices and rebuilding shortlist should be cheaper than sorting Person objects with dict-lookup keys.
asi.rollback_reason: Extra index mapping and rebuild overhead outweighed any sorting simplification.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep original shortlist person list + position-key sort approach.

description: Applied local-binding micro-optimizations in _compat_member_task_values (cache alias, member id alias, cache write through local) to reduce global lookups in this hotspot, but runtime regressed.

asi.hypothesis: Local aliases in _compat_member_task_values hit path should shave lookup overhead across many cache accesses.
asi.rollback_reason: Micro-binding changes did not help and slowed end-to-end performance.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the original simpler _compat_member_task_values implementation.

description: Tried transposing member_task_values with `zip(*member_task_values)` in _compat_member_task_analysis to reduce nested row indexing in per-task scans, but Ruff failed on missing `strict=` and the benchmark trend was slower anyway.

asi.hypothesis: Column-oriented iteration in _compat_member_task_analysis should lower indexing overhead in the hotspot.
asi.rollback_reason: Lint failure (B905 zip strict) blocked validation; measured runtime also regressed relative to best.
asi.next_action_hint: Even if retried with strict=True, this transpose approach is unlikely to beat the current row-index loop.

description: Refactored _compat_member_priority_order rich path to precompute per-member ranking tuples into a list, sort that list once, and return member indices (instead of sorted(range(...), key=...)); this regressed.

asi.hypothesis: Precomputing rich ranking tuples and sorting once should reduce key-function overhead in _compat_member_priority_order.
asi.rollback_reason: Extra tuple/list materialization and broader refactor overhead outweighed saved key-function calls.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep existing sorted(range, key=rich_first_priority_key, reverse=True) implementation.

description: In candidate_combinations scored top-k loop, replaced Python-level `if entry > ranked[0]: heapreplace(...)` gate with unconditional `heapq.heappushpop(...)` after heap fill, to push comparison into C, but this regressed.

asi.hypothesis: heappushpop could reduce Python branching/comparison overhead once the top-k heap is full.
asi.rollback_reason: Unconditional heappushpop did extra heap work for non-competitive entries and slowed runtime.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep explicit `entry > ranked[0]` gate with heapreplace.

description: In candidate_social_potential, precomputed explicit preference IDs for the focal person and reused a prebuilt `{person.id}` set so only teammate-side checks call has_explicit_social_preferences; this significantly regressed runtime.

asi.hypothesis: Eliminating repeated scans of `person.preferences` for each teammate should reduce social-potential hotspot cost.
asi.rollback_reason: Building per-person sets and mixed check paths increased overhead more than expected.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep original symmetric helper calls in candidate_social_potential.

description: Added per-task mapping from candidate tuple object id to scored allocation during combination_scorer evaluation in build_scored_candidates/greedy_allocations, then reused those scored objects when iterating returned candidates to avoid second cached_score_team calls. This regressed.

asi.hypothesis: candidate_combinations and subsequent loops share tuple objects, so reusing first-pass scored allocations by object id should avoid repeated score-cache canonicalization/lookups.
asi.rollback_reason: Extra object-id dictionary bookkeeping and lookup overhead outweighed saved cached_score_team calls.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep existing simple rescoring via cached_score_team hit path.

description: Added request-scoped team-signature cache keyed by `id(people)` (with object-identity guard) so score_team can reuse precomputed `tuple(sorted(member.id ...))` for repeated people tuple objects, but this regressed significantly.

asi.hypothesis: Since score_team sees high repetition of the same people tuple objects, caching team_signature by tuple object identity should remove many repeated ID sorts.
asi.rollback_reason: Extra cache lookup/guard bookkeeping outweighed saved team-signature sorts.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep direct team_signature construction in score_team; this cache layer is not beneficial.

description: Added singleton-set fast path in has_explicit_social_preferences (`len(teammate_ids)==1` direct equality check) to speed dominant one-to-one social checks in candidate_social_potential, but this regressed.

asi.hypothesis: Most calls pass singleton teammate sets, so avoiding generic set-membership checks should reduce has_explicit_social_preferences overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Extra branching/iter overhead outweighed any membership simplification.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the existing generic set-membership implementation.

description: Switched shortlist input-order restoration map from person.id keys to object-identity keys (`id(person)`) in candidate_combinations to avoid string-key lookups, but this regressed heavily.

asi.hypothesis: Identity-keyed position maps might be cheaper than string-keyed maps for shortlist sorting.
asi.rollback_reason: id(...) calls and identity-key mapping were significantly slower than the existing string-id approach.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep person.id-based input position mapping in candidate_combinations.

description: Refactored individual_fit to accept pre-resolved Weights from shortlist_scorers (removing per-call resolve_weights inside individual_fit), but this regressed runtime.

asi.hypothesis: Eliminating repeated resolve_weights calls in individual_fit should reduce shortlist scoring overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Signature/plumbing refactor still underperformed the prior implementation in end-to-end benchmark.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep current individual_fit shape; this refactor is not beneficial.

description: Tried canonicalizing people order inside cached_score_team on cache misses (sort by object identity) and then made score_team team_signature use insertion order to avoid per-call signature sorting, but this changed returned allocation member order and broke init-random tie-behavior regressions.

asi.hypothesis: Canonicalizing people once in cached_score_team could eliminate repeated team_signature sorting while preserving scores.
asi.rollback_reason: Behavioral break: score_team outputs now reflect canonicalized member order, violating tests that assert shuffled tie-breaking order preservation.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not reorder `people` before score_team; any signature optimization must keep allocation.people order unchanged.

description: Added memoization cache in weights.resolve_weights keyed by `(alpha,beta,gamma,delta,mode,preset,normalize)` to reuse immutable Weights objects across repeated calls, but this regressed median runtime substantially.

asi.hypothesis: resolve_weights is called tens of thousands of times; returning cached Weights objects should reduce allocations and improve throughput.
asi.rollback_reason: Global cache lookup/management overhead outweighed object-construction savings in this workload.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep resolve_weights uncached; this helper is too lightweight for global memoization.

description: Precomputed compat pairwise explicit-social booleans once per shortlist_scorers call and reused them in candidate_social_potential to avoid repeated has_explicit_social_preferences checks for mirrored pairs, but this regressed.

asi.hypothesis: A per-shortlist pair map should halve explicit-social check work in candidate_social_potential without affecting semantics.
asi.rollback_reason: Building and consulting the pair map introduced more overhead than the repeated direct checks it replaced.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not pursue pair-map precompute in shortlist_scorers; keep direct social check path.

description: Added a global singleton-teammate cache in has_explicit_social_preferences (keyed by member identity + teammate id, with identity guard) to reuse dominant one-to-one social checks in candidate_social_potential, but this regressed.

asi.hypothesis: Most social checks are singleton teammate queries, so caching these boolean results should reduce repeated preference scans.
asi.rollback_reason: Cache lookup/bookkeeping overhead exceeded savings from repeated singleton scans.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep has_explicit_social_preferences stateless; avoid global singleton cache.

description: Attempted to unify score-cache key and team-component signature by using sorted person-id tuple keys and passing a precomputed team_signature into score_team to avoid duplicate sorting, but this changed score_team call signature and broke monkeypatched test stubs.

asi.hypothesis: Sharing a single sorted person-id signature between cached_score_team and score_team should reduce redundant sorting and remain behaviorally identical.
asi.rollback_reason: Added optional score_team parameter (`team_signature`) broke tests that monkeypatch score_team with fixed kwargs.
asi.next_action_hint: Avoid extending score_team signature; if retried, keep signature unchanged and compute shared values internally.

description: Added local method bindings (`seen_ids.__contains__`, `seen_ids.add`) and person_id local extraction in candidate_combinations shortlist dedup loop to reduce repeated attribute lookups, but this regressed.

asi.hypothesis: Local binding of set operations in the shortlist merge loop should shave Python lookup overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Method binding/extra locals did not improve loop throughput and slowed end-to-end runtime.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep straightforward set membership/add operations in candidate_combinations.

description: Attempted to skip shortlist_scorers setup in greedy_allocations when `C(remaining_people, team_size) <= max_candidate_teams` by supplying a trivial scorer (unused by candidate_combinations in this branch), but lint failed on long nested type line and benchmark trend was slower anyway.

asi.hypothesis: For uncapped greedy tasks, avoiding shortlist_scorers should remove unnecessary scorer/potential computation overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Ruff E501 formatting failure plus poor runtime trend made the change non-viable.
asi.next_action_hint: If retried, use a lint-compliant helper function or callable alias and confirm runtime before keeping.

description: Implemented a fixed-size 4-item integer sorting network in cached_score_team for the dominant team-size case to avoid generic sorted() during score-cache key canonicalization, but this regressed.

asi.hypothesis: A compare-swap sorting network for four identities should beat generic Timsort on tiny fixed-size keys.
asi.rollback_reason: Extra Python branching/swaps were slower than built-in sorted() for this hot path.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep generic sorted identity tuple canonicalization in cached_score_team.

description: Added early-return fast path in `_assign_task_skills_compat` for square teams when greedy matching already covers every task with positive assignments (`len(task_skills)==len(team)==len(matched_values)`), skipping uncovered/rescue/perfect-matching checks. This regressed.

asi.hypothesis: When all skills are already positively matched in square-team compat cases, downstream uncovered/rescue/perfect-matching checks are redundant and can be skipped.
asi.rollback_reason: Fast-path branch plus changed control flow did not improve throughput in aggregate benchmark.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep existing `_assign_task_skills_compat` flow; this early-return shortcut is not beneficial.

description: Replaced manual top-k heap maintenance in candidate_combinations scored path with `heapq.nlargest(max_candidate_teams, enumerate(combinations), key=...)` to push ranking selection into stdlib helper, but this regressed.

asi.hypothesis: `heapq.nlargest` might reduce Python-level heap maintenance overhead versus explicit push/replace loop.
asi.rollback_reason: `nlargest` key-function/tuple handling overhead made the scored top-k path slower.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep explicit heappush/heapreplace loop for scored candidate selection.

description: Adjusted `_compat_member_priority_order` rich-first key construction to sort a generator instead of first materializing a list comprehension, aiming to trim temporary list allocation overhead. This regressed.

asi.hypothesis: Eliminating an intermediate list in rich-first priority key generation should reduce allocation overhead in compat assignment ranking.
asi.rollback_reason: Generator-based sorted path was slower than the prior list-comprehension variant in aggregate runtime.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep list-comprehension input for rich-first priority sorted() call.

description: Optimized `_compat_has_perfect_positive_matching` to reuse a tokenized `seen_tasks` array instead of allocating a fresh boolean list for each augmenting-path attempt. End-to-end benchmark regressed.

asi.hypothesis: Eliminating per-member `seen_tasks` list allocations in perfect-matching checks should reduce hot-path overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Token bookkeeping and extra comparisons did not outperform the previous simple list-based approach.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep current augmenting-path implementation; this tokenization variant is slower.

description: Conditioned expensive `_compat_has_perfect_positive_matching` call on `rescued_values` being non-empty in square-team compat path (skip matching check when greedy already positively covered every task). Runtime improved versus other recent attempts but still did not beat current best.

asi.hypothesis: If no rescue values are needed, greedy already established a positive one-to-one cover in square teams, so perfect-matching verification is redundant.
asi.rollback_reason: Despite being faster than many alternatives, end-to-end median remained above incumbent best commit.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep as a possible revisit only if combined with a larger compat-path change that further reduces assignment overhead.
