description: Bound `math.isclose` to a local `isclose` inside `_compat_member_task_analysis` and switched hot comparisons to that local reference to reduce repeated global attribute lookups. This regressed.

asi.hypothesis: Local-binding `math.isclose` should trim overhead in the hottest compat-analysis comparisons.
asi.rollback_reason: Lookup savings were negligible and did not offset added local plumbing in this workload.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep direct `math.isclose` calls in `_compat_member_task_analysis`.

description: Replaced string task-skill tie-break fields with precomputed integer lexical ranks in compat member-priority and candidate-priority tuples (`task_skill_sort_keys`) to reduce string comparisons, but this regressed.

asi.hypothesis: Using integer tie-break keys instead of strings should speed repeated tuple comparisons in `_compat_member_priority_order` and `_assign_task_skills_compat`.
asi.rollback_reason: Extra per-call rank-map construction outweighed any comparison-time savings.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep direct `task_skill_ids` string tie-break fields unless sort-key preprocessing can be amortized across many calls.

description: Introduced an uncapped-greedy shortcut in `greedy_allocations`: when `C(remaining_people, team_size) <= max_candidate_teams`, skip `shortlist_scorers` and pass a zero scorer (unused by candidate_combinations early-return branch). This regressed substantially.

asi.hypothesis: Avoiding shortlist scorer construction for tasks that already enumerate all combinations should remove unnecessary per-task potential calculations.
asi.rollback_reason: Extra branch/combination counting plus altered control flow produced worse overall runtime despite seeming to skip work.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not reattempt this uncapped shortcut in current shape; keep direct shortlist_scorers path.

description: Rewrote `_compat_member_task_analysis` outer scan to iterate task columns via `enumerate(zip(*member_task_values))` instead of per-member indexing (`task_values[task_index]`), aiming to reduce indexing overhead. This regressed and failed Ruff B905 (`zip` strictness requirement).

asi.hypothesis: Column-wise iteration with `zip(*member_task_values)` could cut inner-loop indexing overhead in compat analysis.
asi.rollback_reason: Performance regressed heavily and lint policy requires explicit `strict=` on zip usage.
asi.next_action_hint: Avoid this zip-based rewrite; any future column iteration must satisfy B905 and justify overhead.

description: In `_compat_fill_uncovered_assignments`, moved `max_skills_per_member` earlier and added no-uncovered fast path that returns assignments directly when `max_skills_per_member==1` (avoiding `_compat_sort_member_assignments` on single-item lists). This regressed.

asi.hypothesis: Sorting per-member assignment lists is unnecessary when each member can hold at most one skill, so skipping sort in the no-uncovered case should reduce overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Added branch/reordered flow did not improve performance and slowed benchmark.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep existing no-uncovered path with `_compat_sort_member_assignments`; this singleton shortcut is not worthwhile.

description: Refactored compat analysis to also compute per-member positive task-index lists and reused them in `_compat_member_priority_order` to avoid re-scanning full member task vectors. Initial attempt failed type checking due outdated empty-return arity.

asi.hypothesis: Computing positive task indices once in `_compat_member_task_analysis` and reusing them should remove repeated `if value > 0` scans in priority ordering.
asi.rollback_reason: Refactor had a ty type error (`_compat_member_task_analysis` empty-path return missing new tuple element).
asi.next_action_hint: Retry with corrected empty-return shape and re-benchmark.

description: Retried and fixed the compat refactor that computes per-member positive task-index lists once in `_compat_member_task_analysis` and reuses them in `_compat_member_priority_order` (eliminating repeated full-vector `value > 0` scans). Checks passed but runtime regressed.

asi.hypothesis: Reusing precomputed positive task indices should reduce repeated scan work in compat priority ordering.
asi.rollback_reason: Extra list/tuple construction in analysis outweighed savings from reduced scan conditions.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not add positive-index list materialization in this path; look for reductions that avoid new per-call allocations.

description: Added an early-return in `_compat_sort_member_assignments` that skips task-order sorting when every member has 0/1 assigned skills (sorting would be a no-op). End-to-end runtime still regressed.

asi.hypothesis: Many compat assignments are singleton per member, so bypassing redundant sorted() calls should cut `_compat_fill_uncovered_assignments` overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Extra pre-check branch/all() scan outweighed savings from skipped tiny sort calls.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep direct sort path; singleton-noop detection is not profitable here.

description: Added a dedicated singleton helper `has_explicit_social_preference_for_teammate(member, teammate_id)` and used it in `candidate_social_potential` to avoid allocating `{teammate_id}` sets on every COMPAT pair check. This still regressed.

asi.hypothesis: Avoiding per-call singleton set construction in social-explicit checks should reduce candidate_social_potential overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Extra helper call/dispatch overhead outweighed savings from removing tiny set allocations.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep existing set-based explicit-social check path; singleton helper split is not beneficial.

description: Threaded precomputed `uncovered_skill_ids` from `_assign_task_skills_compat` into `_compat_fill_uncovered_assignments` to avoid rebuilding assigned-count/uncovered-scan state in every return path. This regressed.

asi.hypothesis: Reusing already-known uncovered task IDs should remove repeated dictionary/count scans inside `_compat_fill_uncovered_assignments`.
asi.rollback_reason: Added plumbing/list materialization across all paths outweighed the avoided recomputation.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep `_compat_fill_uncovered_assignments` self-contained; this uncovered-threading refactor is not profitable.

description: Retested gating `_compat_has_perfect_positive_matching` behind `rescued_values` in square-team compat assignment (skip matching check when greedy already produced full positive cover). Repeat run remained ~143.7ms and still above incumbent best.

asi.hypothesis: Perfect-matching verification is redundant when no rescue values were needed in square-team compat assignments.
asi.rollback_reason: Consistent improvement versus many recent trials but still not enough to beat incumbent best commit metric.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep this as a combination candidate only if paired with additional compat-path reductions; alone it is insufficient.

description: Precomputed per-person explicit teammate-id sets once in shortlist_scorers and used set membership in candidate_social_potential (instead of repeated has_explicit_social_preferences scans) for COMPAT social gating. This regressed.

asi.hypothesis: Precomputing explicit-preference ID sets should reduce repeated preference-list scans in candidate_social_potential.
asi.rollback_reason: Building and consulting per-person sets added overhead that outweighed direct list-scan checks.
asi.next_action_hint: Avoid explicit-preference set precomputation in shortlist_scorers.

description: Introduced `_top_partner_mean` with fixed-size top-k fast paths (k=1/2/3) and replaced full `sorted(..., reverse=True)[:k]` in candidate social/personality potentials. This regressed.

asi.hypothesis: Avoiding full list sorts for tiny partner counts should reduce shortlist potential-scoring overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Manual top-k logic added Python branching overhead and was slower than built-in sorted for these small lists.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep existing sorted-slice implementation for candidate potentials.

description: Switched request-scoped personality/social component cache signatures from sorted member-id strings to sorted member object identities (`tuple[int, ...]`) to avoid string sorting/comparison in score_team cache keys. This regressed.

asi.hypothesis: Integer identity signatures for team-component caches should be cheaper than string-id signatures while preserving per-request correctness.
asi.rollback_reason: Identity-signature construction/lookup did not outperform existing string-signature path.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep team-component cache keys based on member.id signatures.

description: Tried a greedy-selection redesign: when candidate_combinations already used scored ranking (`total_candidates > max_candidate_teams`), evaluate candidates only until quality drops below the top score and apply deterministic tie-break only within that top-quality prefix. Initial version failed Ruff E501 and benchmark trend regressed.

asi.hypothesis: For non-random capped tasks, candidate_combinations returns quality-sorted candidates, so rescoring all candidates in greedy_allocations is unnecessary; only top-quality ties need evaluation.
asi.rollback_reason: Implementation failed lint (E501) and showed slower runtime trend.
asi.next_action_hint: If retried, keep lint-safe formatting and validate that prefix-only rescoring actually reduces overhead before broader adoption.

description: Tried reducing `math.isclose` calls in `_compat_member_task_analysis` by adding exact-equality short-circuits (`value == best_value`) before tolerance checks and applying the same pattern in `other_member_best_values` construction. This regressed heavily.

asi.hypothesis: Many task values are exactly equal (especially 0.0), so short-circuiting equality before `math.isclose` should cut hot-path tolerance checks.
asi.rollback_reason: Extra branching/boolean logic increased overhead more than it reduced `math.isclose` usage.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the original concise `math.isclose` conditions in compat analysis.

description: Replaced scored top-k heap maintenance in `candidate_combinations` with full materialize+sort of all scored shortlist combinations, then sliced top `max_candidate_teams`. This regressed.

asi.hypothesis: When shortlist combination count is near cap, a single full sort may beat repeated Python-level heappush/heapreplace operations.
asi.rollback_reason: Materializing and sorting the full scored list was slower than incremental heap selection.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep heap-based top-k path in `candidate_combinations` for scored ranking.

description: Tried a broader shortlist redesign by disabling alternate scorer ranked lists when `combination_scorer` is present (scored capped path), keeping only primary scorer ordering before combination ranking. This regressed heavily.

asi.hypothesis: In scored capped search, alternate shortlist rankings may be redundant because combination_scorer re-ranks teams anyway; dropping alternates should reduce shortlist sorting overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Alternate-ranked shortlist diversity appears performance-critical; removing it degraded end-to-end runtime substantially.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not disable alternate_scorers in scored candidate_combinations path.

description: Added optional `ranked_output` capture in `candidate_combinations` and used it in non-random `greedy_allocations` to select the best candidate from top-quality ties without rescoring every returned candidate; fallback rescoring remains for random mode and unranked paths. This regressed.

asi.hypothesis: Reusing candidate_combinations' computed quality ordering should remove many redundant cached_score_team calls in greedy selection.
asi.rollback_reason: Extra ranked-output plumbing/signature scans outweighed saved rescoring lookups in this workload.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not add ranked-output side channel to candidate_combinations in current form.

description: Rewrote `_task_preference_score` to avoid geometric_mean generator/list overhead: return `compat_default` directly when no task preferences and otherwise compute log-sum in a direct loop with early zero guard. This improved over many recent trials but still missed incumbent best.

asi.hypothesis: `_task_preference_score` is hot; direct log-sum and constant-default fast path should reduce geometric_mean overhead without changing semantics.
asi.rollback_reason: Despite a decent gain, median runtime remained above current best commit.
asi.next_action_hint: Consider combining this task-preference fast path with a separate compat-assignment reduction in one experiment.

description: Refactored `improve_allocations` trial evaluation to compute objective deltas from cached quality aggregates (product/min/sum) instead of rebuilding `trial_allocations` and re-running `allocation_objective` on each attempted swap/replacement. This was a strong relative gain vs recent attempts but still above incumbent best.

asi.hypothesis: Avoiding repeated list copies and full objective recomputation inside swap loops should reduce improve_allocations overhead without changing swap decisions.
asi.rollback_reason: Despite a sizable speedup versus recent variants, median runtime still did not beat the existing best kept commit.
asi.next_action_hint: Potentially combine this objective-delta approach with other independent wins; standalone it is insufficient.

description: Combined three previously promising reductions: (1) `_task_preference_score` direct fast path/log loop, (2) gate square-team `_compat_has_perfect_positive_matching` behind non-empty `rescued_values`, and (3) objective-delta trial evaluation in `improve_allocations` to avoid per-trial allocation copies/objective recomputation. Combined result improved strongly but still did not beat incumbent best.

asi.hypothesis: These near-win changes target independent hotspots (_task_preference_score, compat perfect-matching checks, and swap objective evaluation) and should stack to exceed any single-change gain.
asi.rollback_reason: Even combined, median metric remained above current best kept run.
asi.next_action_hint: If revisited, pair this bundle with a genuinely new candidate-generation/compat-analysis reduction rather than more micro-tweaks.

description: Reworked scored top-k heap entries in `candidate_combinations` to store integer combination indices (`(score, -index, index)`) plus a side `all_combinations` list, avoiding tuple[Person,...] objects in heap comparisons. This regressed.

asi.hypothesis: Using integer-backed heap entries should reduce comparison overhead in top-k maintenance versus carrying full combination tuples.
asi.rollback_reason: Extra side-list append/index indirection outweighed any heap-comparison savings.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep direct `(score, -index, combination)` heap entries.

description: Removed precomputed `other_member_best_values` matrix allocation from `_compat_member_task_analysis`; now it returns best/second-best/count vectors, and `_assign_task_skills_compat` computes `other_member_best` lazily per candidate task during priority evaluation. This improved significantly but remained above incumbent best.

asi.hypothesis: Eliminating per-call member×task matrix materialization should reduce compat-analysis overhead, especially since assignment loop only needs a subset of entries.
asi.rollback_reason: Despite strong relative improvement, median still did not beat best kept commit.
asi.next_action_hint: Consider combining this lazy-other-member-best approach with another independent compat-path reduction.

description: Combined four independent hotspot reductions into one patchset: (1) `_task_preference_score` direct fast path/log loop (avoids geometric_mean generator/list overhead), (2) square-team compat perfect-matching check gated behind non-empty `rescued_values`, (3) `_compat_member_task_analysis` no longer materializes `other_member_best_values` matrix (lazy per-candidate computation in `_assign_task_skills_compat`), and (4) `improve_allocations` uses objective-delta math instead of per-trial list-copy+allocation_objective recomputation. This produced a clear new best while preserving quality metrics/checks.

asi.hypothesis: Stacking several near-win, behavior-preserving reductions across independent hot paths should compound into a true end-to-end win.
asi.observed_effect: Large cumulative speedup with unchanged quality metrics and passing checks.

description: Inlined singleton explicit-social checks directly inside `candidate_social_potential` (removed set construction and `has_explicit_social_preferences` helper calls for COMPAT pair gating). This regressed versus new best.

asi.hypothesis: Direct inline preference scans should reduce per-pair social-gating overhead versus helper+singleton-set calls.
asi.rollback_reason: Expanded inline loops/branching were slower than the existing helper-based approach in aggregate.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep current helper-based social gating.

description: In `_assign_task_skills_compat`, avoided `_compat_fill_uncovered_assignments` full assigned-count/uncovered scan when `covered_mask` already covers all task skills: use direct `_compat_sort_member_assignments` in no-uncovered path and reuse a single `finalized_assignments` object across subsequent return branches. This regressed vs current best.

asi.hypothesis: Many compat teams have no uncovered skills; bypassing `_compat_fill_uncovered_assignments` in that case should cut redundant counting/scanning work.
asi.rollback_reason: Despite a decent runtime, this path still underperformed the current kept baseline.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep current unified finalize path unless paired with broader `_compat_fill_uncovered_assignments` redesign.

description: Optimized the new objective-delta `improve_allocations` path by precomputing per-round helper data (`clamped_qualities`, `min_without_index`, and per-pair `other_min`) so inner swap/replacement loops avoid repeated per-trial scans and repeated `max(..., 1e-12)` work. This produced a further best with checks/quality unchanged.

asi.hypothesis: After moving to objective deltas, remaining overhead is repeated min/product support work inside inner loops; precomputing those per round should compound the gain.
asi.observed_effect: Additional measurable win on top of prior keep.

description: Special-cased `_compat_fill_uncovered_assignments` for `max_skills_per_member==1` earlier in the flow: compute `max_skills_per_member` up front and return assignments directly when no uncovered skills (skipping `_compat_sort_member_assignments`), while preserving duplicate-skill count handling. This regressed.

asi.hypothesis: Dominant square-team compat case has one skill per member, so bypassing no-op sort/extra branch work in `_compat_fill_uncovered_assignments` should reduce overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Restructured branching and earlier max-skills handling slowed the overall path despite the singleton fast path.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep `_compat_fill_uncovered_assignments` structure from 13df519; singleton early-return tweak is not beneficial.

description: In `improve_allocations` replacement phase, replaced repeated `list(unused_people)` creation with a per-allocation immutable snapshot (`tuple(unused_people)`) to reduce loop allocation churn. This regressed strongly.

asi.hypothesis: Avoiding repeated list copies in inner replacement loops should reduce overhead after objective-delta refactor.
asi.rollback_reason: Tuple snapshot creation/iteration pattern performed worse than existing list copy approach in this workload.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep `list(unused_people)` iteration in replacement loops.

description: Retried uncapped-task greedy shortcut with a materially different approach: bypassed `shortlist_scorers`/`candidate_combinations` entirely when `C(remaining_people, team_size) <= max_candidate_teams` by directly enumerating `itertools.combinations`. This showed slower trend and hit Ruff E501 formatting.

asi.hypothesis: Direct combination enumeration in uncapped tasks should remove unnecessary scorer setup and candidate_combinations overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Benchmark regressed and lint failed due long combination_scorer lambda line.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not pursue uncapped greedy shortcut further without clear profiling evidence; prior variants consistently regress.

description: Replaced `_compat_member_task_analysis` and related assignment-path `math.isclose` comparisons with exact float equality checks (`==`) to remove tolerance-call overhead. This regressed heavily.

asi.hypothesis: Compat task values are sourced directly from member skill levels, so exact equality might be sufficient and faster than repeated `math.isclose` calls.
asi.rollback_reason: Exact-equality path performed substantially worse despite fewer tolerance calls.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep `math.isclose` logic in compat analysis/priority tie handling.

description: In `candidate_combinations`, replaced shortlist reordering via `input_positions` dict + `shortlist.sort(key=...)` with direct input-order reconstruction using set membership (`[person for person in people if person.id in seen_ids]`). This preserves ordering semantics while removing per-call key-dict construction and sort overhead; produced a strong new best.

asi.hypothesis: For small people lists, a single linear pass over original order with set membership may be cheaper than building a position map and sorting shortlist by key.
asi.observed_effect: Large end-to-end win with checks and quality metrics unchanged.

description: Follow-up shortlist tweak: removed intermediate shortlist list maintenance during round-robin selection (track only `selected_count` + `seen_ids`, then reconstruct shortlist from original people order). This regressed strongly versus current best.

asi.hypothesis: If shortlist is reconstructed at the end anyway, skipping per-add list appends should reduce overhead further.
asi.rollback_reason: List-append removal plus count-tracking/branch changes unexpectedly slowed the hot loop.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep explicit shortlist append path together with final input-order reconstruction.

description: Added a `len(team)==4` fast path in `_task_preference_score` with direct 4-value retrieval/log computation to avoid generic loop overhead on benchmark-dominant team size. This regressed.

asi.hypothesis: Specializing task-preference geometric mean for fixed team size 4 should reduce per-call loop overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Extra branching/specialized path overhead outweighed savings from fixed-size unrolling.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep generic loop implementation in `_task_preference_score`.

description: Refactored `_compat_member_priority_order` to precompute `(priority_key..., member_index)` rows and sort once, eliminating nested key-function definitions/callback overhead. This regressed and failed type checking due overly-generic tuple typing (`list[object]` return inference).

asi.hypothesis: Building sortable rows explicitly may reduce per-call key-function overhead in hot compat priority ordering.
